note: Same assessment as the previous day's call in this sequence, now with the income miss confirmed by evidence rather than inference: he went away, checked, and came back with a hard ceiling - $150 to $175 available and no more than roughly $1,500 obtainable on credit. Health remains a crisis rather than a neglected area, at 230 lb and 5'7" with a stated fear of heart attack and stroke, and the starting point remains rescue rather than good-to-great in his own framing. He is not gym-averse, having trained on and off since he was thirteen, but he is squarely inside the exclusion the ICP words as being fifty pounds overweight. Successful is arguable and left in neither array: a licensed Medicare insurance agent is a real career but not the business-owner-or-physician profile, and the household finances contradict his own description of making good money again. What this call adds to the ICP question is his verdict on the price itself - 'I personally think it's too much, but I believe in it' - which is a different signal from cannot afford, and one worth separating in the rollup.
